chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the 'Aqiqa, is it obligatory? He said, 'Yes, it is obligatory.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah: A common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: Aqiqa: The ritual sacrifice of an animal made on behalf of a newborn child.
key_terms.وَاجِبَةٌ: Obligatory: A legal ruling indicating a mandatory act whose omission is sinful.

ai.seo_question: Is the Aqiqa sacrifice for a newborn child obligatory in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explicitly confirms that the 'Aqiqa sacrifice is an obligatory act (wajib), distinguishing it from mere recommendation (mustahabb) in this specific legal context. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it underscores the ritual gratitude owed to Allah for the birth of a child, linking the physical act of sacrifice to spiritual purification and the fulfillment of a divine duty.
